Free and open source. macOS 12 or later, Apple silicon or Intel.

Any format. No converting.

FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3, AAC, OGG and Opus all play straight through, with artwork, artists and album order intact. Nothing is re-encoded and nothing is copied into a second library — the files stay exactly as you ripped or bought them.

Music on, music off.

Choose the albums you want and see exactly how much room is left before you commit. Taking tracks off is just as easy. No sync dialog decides what lives on your iPod.

Rockbox, start to finish.

Format the iPod, install Rockbox, add the bootloader, then browse hundreds of themes with real previews filtered to your model — the whole job in one window. The Classic install is confirmed working on real hardware.

Every theme, previewed before you commit.

The whole Rockbox catalogue — 735 themes for the iPod Video alone — filtered so you only ever see skins built for your model. Install one with a click. The themes already on your iPod switch instantly, with no download and no digging through menus on the device.

It looks the way you remember.

Brushed metal, the green display, Cover Flow you can flick through with two fingers. Your library sits in a source list, exactly where it used to.

Or turn the whole window into an iPod Classic and drive it with a click wheel you can actually spin.

Where it stands today

It's early, and some of this touches your iPod's firmware. Here's exactly what's finished and what isn't, so you can decide what to plug in.

Playing your library

Ready Lossless playback, artwork, Cover Flow, artist and album browsing, and the iPod Classic window.

Themes and music

Ready On an iPod already running Rockbox: browse, install and switch themes; add and remove albums; see real free space.

Installing Rockbox
iPod Classic

Confirmed Working on real hardware. The bootloader install has been run successfully on an iPod Classic 7th generation. It goes over USB, needs no administrator password, and if it fails the iPod stays in DFU mode where Finder can restore it.

Installing Rockbox
older iPods

In testing The 1st–5.5G, mini, nano and Colour models take a different route — a write to the firmware partition — and that path isn't confirmed on hardware yet. Your existing firmware is backed up first and the install stops if that backup fails, but don't use an iPod you'd be upset to lose.

Formatting the iPod

Ready Reformats the music partition as FAT32, the only format Rockbox can read. No Windows PC needed — “MS-DOS (FAT32)” is simply what Apple calls it.

Original Apple software

Not yet An iPod still running Apple's firmware can be recognised, but not loaded with music. Rockbox has to be installed first.

Requirements

macOS 12 (Monterey) or later. Universal — runs natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. The build isn't notarised yet, so the first launch needs one extra step — see Opening it the first time.

iPod Classic, 6th and 7th generation. Fully supported in the app now, including the bootloader — it walks you through the DFU button hold and writes it over USB. This is the one install route confirmed working on real hardware.

Opening it the first time

This build isn't notarised by Apple yet, so macOS will say it “could not verify iPod Connect is free of malware.” That's the warning every unsigned app gets, not a finding about this one. Choose Done — never Move to Trash — then:

  1. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security
  2. Scroll down to “iPod Connect was blocked” and click Open Anyway
  3. Launch the app again and confirm

Or one line in Terminal does the same thing:
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/iPod Connect.app"
